text: {A}, do your best impression of a Disney character. Group votes thumbs up or down. Majority down: drink 3.
{A}, text someone you haven't spoken to in over a year. Everyone else picks who you text. Do it: hand out 3 sips. Refuse: drink 3.
{A}, let the person to your left post anything they want to your Instagram story. Do it: give out 4 sips. Refuse: drink 4.
{A}, speak only in questions for the next 2 minutes. Every time you slip up, drink 1.
{A}, read out the last voice message you received. If you refuse, drink 3.
{A}, show the group your most recent photo in your camera roll without previewing it. Drink 2 if it's embarrassing.
{A}, name 5 countries in 10 seconds. Miss one: drink 2.
{A}, tell the group a rumour about yourself that's actually true. Group decides how many sips it's worth (1–4).
{A}, take a sip for every country you've visited. Cap at 5.
{A}, do 10 seconds of your best TikTok dance. Group gives a score out of 10 — that's how many sips you hand out.
{A}, change your phone wallpaper to a photo the group chooses — keep it until the next card draw. Refuse: drink 3.
{A}, for the next round you must refer to yourself in the third person. Every slip costs you 1 sip.
{A}, read the last thing you searched on Google out loud. Drink 2 if it's something you'd rather not share.
{A}, give a one-minute stand-up comedy bit about university life. If the group laughs at least once, you hand out 3 sips.
{A}, send a voice note to someone in your contacts saying "I miss you." Do it: give 3 sips. Refuse: drink 3.
{A}, let the group scroll through your Spotify recently played. Drink 1 for every guilty pleasure they find.
{A}, say a word. Go around clockwise naming songs with that word in the title. First person to fail drinks 2.
{A}, reveal how many people in this room you've told a secret to. Drink that many sips.
{A}, hold a straight face while the rest of the group tries to make you laugh for 30 seconds. Fail: drink 2.
{A}, you have 20 seconds to name the capitals of 5 different countries. Miss any: drink 2.
{A}, add a stranger on Instagram right now. Do it: hand out 3 sips. Refuse: drink 3.
{A}, dramatically re-enact the last argument you had. Keep going until the group claps. Drink 1 per 10 seconds of silence.
{A}, say something nice about the person to your right — but make it sound like an insult. Drink 2 if they look confused.
{A}, show the group the last meme you saved. If nobody laughs: drink 2.
{A}, name your three most-used apps. For every one the group guessed correctly before you revealed it, drink 1.
{A}, pick a person in the group and describe their vibe using only movie or TV show titles. If they agree, hand out 3. If not, drink 2.
{A}, do your best accent from a country you've never visited. Group rates it out of 5 — that's how many sips you give out.
{A}, everyone in the group gives you a one-word description of your personality. Drink 1 for each word you disagree with.
{A}, you have 15 seconds to freestyle rap about what happened today. Fail to start: drink 2.
{A}, take the group on a 60-second tour of your camera roll starting from one year ago today. Drink 1 for every photo you skip.
{A}, tell the group the most embarrassing thing in your search history right now. Drink 3 if you refuse.
{A}, walk around the room like you're on a fashion runway for 15 seconds. Group scores you — give out that many sips (max 5).
{A}, confess a food opinion you know will be controversial. Anyone who loudly disagrees drinks 1.
{A}, you can ask anyone in the group a question they must answer honestly — or drink 3.
{A}, describe your love life using only a weather forecast. Drink 2 if people laugh at the forecast.
{A}, open your most recent chat and read the last message you sent out loud. Drink 2 if it's cringe.
{A}, pick the person you think is most likely to become famous. Tell them why — they give out 2 sips if they like it, drink 2 if they don't.
{A}, without using your hands, mime the plot of any movie until someone guesses it. Give out 3 sips to the one who gets it.
{A}, assign a Hogwarts house to everyone in the group and explain your reasoning. Anyone who disagrees with their assignment drinks 1.
{A}, scroll to a random contact and do an impression of how they talk. If nobody guesses who it is: drink 2.
{A}, turn your phone screen brightness to maximum and show the group your lock screen wallpaper. Drink 1 if someone comments on it.
{A}, choose someone to be your lawyer. Reveal a minor crime you've committed (parking, speeding, etc.). If your lawyer can argue you innocent in 30 seconds, give out 3 sips. If not, drink 2.
{A}, talk for 30 seconds about a topic the person to your left picks — without pausing, repeating yourself, or going off topic. Fail: drink 2.
{A}, type and send a message to your mum or dad saying "I need to talk to you about something important." Do it: give 4 sips. Refuse: drink 4.
{A}, guess everyone's screen time average for last week. For each correct guess (within 30 min): give out 1 sip.
{A}, write a two-sentence bio for yourself as though you were on a dating app. Read it aloud. Drink 1 if anyone cringes.
{A}, do your best impression of one person in this room — without saying their name. First person to guess correctly gets 2 sips to give out.
{A}, tell a joke. If nobody laughs: drink 2. If everyone laughs: give out 4 sips.
{A}, share a screenshot from your camera roll taken in the last 48 hours. If the group finds it boring, drink 1.
{A}, convince the group you have a totally made-up skill in 30 seconds. If the majority believes you: give out 3 sips. If not: drink 2.
Anyone who has matched with someone on a dating app and never sent the first message — drink 2.
If you've ever ghosted someone who did nothing wrong — drink 2.
Drink 1 for every language you can introduce yourself in.
If you've ever lied about having seen a movie everyone else has watched — drink 2.
If you've ever binged an entire Netflix season in one day — drink 1.
Anyone who has cried at a Disney movie as an adult — drink 1.
If you've ever sent a risky text and immediately regretted it — drink 2.
If your screen time last week was over 6 hours per day — drink 2.
If you've ever eavesdropped on a stranger's conversation and genuinely got invested — drink 1.
Anyone who has stayed in a relationship longer than they should have — drink 2.
If you've ever pretended to be busy to avoid a social event — drink 1.
If you've paid for a subscription you haven't used in the past month — drink 1.
Anyone who has googled themselves — drink 1. Drink an extra if you liked what you found.
If you've ever skipped class and then felt guilty about it the whole day anyway — drink 1.
If you've ever liked someone's photo from years ago while stalking their profile — drink 2.
If you've ever used "I'm five minutes away" when you were still at home — drink 2.
Anyone who has bought something online while drunk — drink 2. Drink an extra if you don't regret it.
If you've ever muted someone on social media without unfollowing them — drink 1.
If you still know all the words to a song from when you were 12 — drink 1.
If you've ever gone on a date just to have something to do — drink 2.
Anyone who has cried on public transport — drink 1.
If you've ever ordered pizza at 2am completely sober — drink 1.
Drink 1 for every city you've lived in.
If you've ever rehearsed a phone call before making it — drink 1.
Anyone who has changed their outfit more than twice before going out tonight — drink 2.
If you've ever read a whole thread of drama about strangers online and felt emotionally involved — drink 1.
If you've ever had a crush on someone you met while travelling — drink 1.
If you've ever written a very detailed complaint you never sent — drink 1.
Anyone who has pretended not to see someone in public to avoid talking to them — drink 1.
If you've ever slept past noon on a weekday — drink 1.
If you've told someone "I'll explain later" and never actually explained — drink 2.
Anyone who has left a text on read on purpose to seem busy — drink 2.
If you've ever made up an elaborate excuse to leave a party early — drink 1.
If you've argued about a film or show you haven't actually finished watching — drink 2.
Anyone who has laughed at someone else's joke so they'd stop telling it — drink 1.
If you've looked up the menu of a restaurant before going, just to know what you're getting — drink 1.
If you've ever had a full conversation with your pet, fully expecting answers — drink 1.
If you've ever rewritten a text message more than three times before sending — drink 2.
Anyone who is in a group chat they've muted for over 6 months — drink 1.
If you've ever stayed awake just because you didn't want to stop watching something — drink 1.
If you've ever immediately checked your phone after putting it down because it felt empty — drink 1.
Anyone who has ever sent the wrong text to the wrong person — drink 2. Drink an extra if it was about that person.
If you've ever laughed at your own joke before finishing it — drink 1.
If you've borrowed money and taken longer than planned to pay it back — drink 2.
If you've ever been the only person in a group chat who didn't see the message — drink 1.
{STARTER} starts: name a country. Go clockwise naming countries. No repeats, no pausing. First person to fail drinks 2.
Vote: Would you rather have unlimited free flights or free accommodation anywhere in the world? Minority votes drinks 2.
Everyone points at the person they think is most likely to become a reality TV star. The most-pointed-at person drinks 2.
{STARTER} begins a story with one sentence. Go clockwise, each person adds one sentence. Anyone who ruins the narrative drinks 2.
Everyone raises their glass and says one genuine compliment to the group. Last person to speak drinks 2.
Vote: Would you rather have perfect memory or never need sleep? Minority drinks 2.
{STARTER} names a celebrity. Everyone must name someone that celebrity could plausibly be dating. Most creative answer (group vote) gives out 3 sips.
Everyone simultaneously points at the person in the group most likely to still be awake at 5am. Most pointed-at person drinks 2.
Speed round: everyone names a TV show they've watched in the last week. Anyone who can't think of one drinks 2.
{STARTER} hums the intro to a song. First person to guess it gives out 2 sips. {STARTER} drinks 2 if nobody guesses within 30 seconds.
Point at who you think is the best dancer in the group. Most votes: you must prove it with a 15-second solo. Skip: drink 3.
Everyone votes for the person most likely to move abroad permanently. Most votes: give out 3 sips.
{STARTER} picks a category (e.g. "Marvel movies"). Go clockwise naming things in that category. Repeat or hesitate: drink 2.
Everyone on 3 holds up a number of fingers between 1 and 5. Anyone whose number nobody else chose drinks 2.
Vote: would you rather lose all your photos or all your contacts? Minority drinks 2. Ties: everyone drinks 1.
{STARTER} gives a 30-second TED talk on a random topic they make up on the spot. Group rates 1–5 — that's how many sips they give out.
Everyone texts their best friend the same message: "Can I tell you something weird?" The most interesting reply wins — that person gives out 3 sips.
Everyone points at who they'd call first in a crisis. Most pointed-at: give out 3 sips. Nobody points at you: drink 2.
Group vote: who in this room has the best fashion sense? Runner-up drinks 1. Last place drinks 3.

{STARTER} whispers a word to the person on their left. That person adds a word and whispers the two-word phrase to the next person, and so on. Read out the final phrase — funniest result: {STARTER} gives out 3 sips.
Everyone stands up. Name a movie genre. Sit down if you've watched that genre this month. Last person standing drinks 2.
Group decides: most likely to accidentally start a rumour. That person drinks 2 and must confirm or deny with a story.
{STARTER} picks two people in the group and makes a case for why they'd be a great couple. Those two people rate the pitch out of 5 — {STARTER} gives out that many sips combined.
Everyone simultaneously shouts out their ranking of the best city they've visited. Anyone alone in their top pick gives out 2 sips.
Vote: Is a hot dog a sandwich? Yes or No. Minority drinks 2. Anyone who refuses to vote drinks 3.
Everyone simultaneously names their biggest red flag in a relationship. Most relatable answer (group vote): give out 3 sips.
Everyone secretly writes a country they want to live in and reveals at the same time. Anyone who wrote the same country as someone else: give each other 1 sip.
Group vote: who is the best liar? That person must prove it by bluffing convincingly about what they had for lunch. Group decides if they believe them.
{STARTER} names a number (1–10). Everyone who rates tonight higher than that number gives out 1 sip. Everyone who rates it lower drinks 1.
Name the last song you had stuck in your head. Go clockwise — anyone who names a song already said must drink 1. Last person with a unique song gives out 3 sips.
Everyone secretly rates themselves 1–10 on their cooking ability. Reveal simultaneously. Biggest overestimator (group opinion) drinks 2.
Everyone points at who they think will be last to go to sleep tonight. Most votes: defend your night owl reputation or drink 2.
Vote: Would you rather always know when people are lying or always know what people are thinking? Minority drinks 2.
Everyone names their comfort food. First duplicate found: both people drink 1. No duplicates: {STARTER} gives out 2 sips.
Everyone holds up fingers showing how many apps they currently have notifications on. Highest number: drink that many sips (max 5).
{A} vs {B}: first to name 10 capital cities wins. Winner gives out 3 sips.
{A} vs {B}: rock-paper-scissors, best of 3. Loser drinks 3.
{A} vs {B}: staring contest. First to blink or laugh drinks 3.
{A} vs {B}: who can hold a plank longer? Loser drinks 3. If neither lasts 15 seconds, both drink.
{A} vs {B}: both guess how many push-ups the other can do right now. Actual number decides who was closer — the further-off guess drinks 2.
{A} vs {B}: both guess the current time without checking your phone. Closest guess gives out 2 sips.
{A} vs {B}: thumb war. Loser drinks 2. If the match lasts more than 30 seconds, both drink 1.
{A} vs {B}: both write down a number between 1 and 100 without showing each other. Reveal simultaneously — closest to 50 wins and gives out 3 sips.
{A} vs {B}: each gives the other a compliment in exactly 10 words. Group votes whose was better — loser drinks 2.
{A} vs {B}: improvised rap battle — one verse each on the topic of "Monday mornings." Group votes. Loser drinks 3.
{A} vs {B}: who can say the most countries in 20 seconds? Loser drinks 2.
{A} vs {B}: 60-second debate — argue opposite sides of "pineapple on pizza." Group decides the winner. Loser drinks 2.
{A} vs {B}: both simultaneously say a number between 1 and 10. If you say the same number, both give out 3 sips. Higher number drinks 2.
{A} vs {B}: both describe their personality using only 3 emojis (show each other's phone screens). Group votes who described themselves most accurately. Loser drinks 2.
{A} vs {B}: mirror each other's movements for 20 seconds. Whoever breaks character first drinks 2.
{A} vs {B}: both claim a skill they think the other person doesn't have. Group votes who's more believable. Loser drinks 2.
{A} vs {B}: both write down how many hours of sleep they got last night. Person with the most gives out 2 sips. Person with the fewest gets sympathy — they hand out 1 sip.
{A} vs {B}: who has the most unread emails right now? Loser drinks 2 and must share the subject of their oldest unread.
{A} vs {B}: both say a word at the same time on 3. If they rhyme, everyone else drinks 1. If they're antonyms, give out 3 each. Otherwise, loser in a word association chain drinks 1.
{A} vs {B}: first to correctly name the year a song came out (group picks the song) wins and gives out 3 sips.
{A} vs {B}: both secretly write down what they think the other person's most-used emoji is. Reveal together — closest guess wins and gives out 2 sips.
{A} vs {B}: tongue-twister race — "She sells seashells by the seashore." Fastest clean run gives out 3 sips.
{A} vs {B}: who has more apps installed on their phone? Loser drinks 2.
{A} vs {B}: both freestyle-describe each other to a stranger in 20 seconds. Group votes the most accurate description. Loser drinks 2.
{A} vs {B}: who can name more Taylor Swift albums in 20 seconds? Loser drinks 2.
Waterfall! Starting from {STARTER}, everyone starts drinking and can't stop until the person to their left stops. {STARTER} stops first.
Social round! Everyone drinks for the group.
Speed round! Go clockwise naming things in the category "things you do at 2am" — any hesitation or repeat drinks 1.
Group choice! Everyone votes for a group dare right now: (a) everyone sends a voice note to a contact, or (b) everyone takes a sip. Majority rules.
Gratitude round. Everyone says something they're grateful for tonight. Anyone who can't think of something drinks 2.
Everyone checks how many steps they've done today. Lowest step count drinks 2.

Chaos! Everyone passes their phone to the left. The person holding it has 5 seconds to type something in the search bar before giving it back. The weirder the better — funniest entry gives out 2 sips.
Everyone stands up and says one honest thing about themselves that the group probably doesn't know. Sit down when you've said it. Last person standing drinks 2.
High-low! Everyone shares their high and low of the week in one sentence each. Most relatable high: give out 2. Most relatable low: receive 2 from the group.
Drink if you've checked your phone in the last 2 minutes. Be honest.
Everyone simultaneously shouts out their current mood in one word. Anyone who says the same word as someone else — both give out 1 sip each.
Free sip! {STARTER} picks one person to drink for no reason at all.
Everyone does a dramatic cheers, says something inspirational (fake or real), and drinks.
Everyone opens their most recent Instagram story viewer list and drinks 1 for every person they recognise but haven't spoken to this month.
Everyone silently points at who they think had the most interesting week. Most pointed-at person must share a two-sentence summary. They give out 2 sips.
Everyone drinks 1 for every continent they have NOT visited.
Everyone simultaneously reveals the last emoji they sent to someone. Person who sent the most chaotic one gives out 2 sips (group vote).
Everyone name one thing you wish was different about tonight's plan — without saying anything negative about a person. Anyone who can't: drink 2.
Group hype moment! Everyone screams their own name loudly on the count of 3. Anyone who hesitates drinks 1.
Everyone pick someone they'd go backpacking with for a month. No repeats — first come first served. Anyone left unpicked drinks 2, the group drinks 1 in their honour.
Last person to like a post on Instagram right now drinks 2.
Last person to stand up drinks 2.
Last person to put their hand on their head drinks 2.
Last person to name a country beginning with the letter M drinks 2.
Last person to open their camera app and take a photo drinks 2.
Last person to say the name of the city you're in right now drinks 2.
Last person to touch the floor with both palms drinks 2.
Last person to switch their phone to silent mode drinks 2.
Last person to point at someone wearing black drinks 2.
Last person to say "cheers" in a language other than English drinks 2.
Last person to make eye contact with someone else in the group and wink drinks 2.
Last person to show their home screen on their phone drinks 2.
Last person to correctly name tomorrow's day of the week drinks 2. (No excuses.)
Last person to sit back down after standing up drinks 2.
Last person to clap their hands twice drinks 2.
New rule: no one can say anyone's real name. Make up a nickname for everyone right now. Use the wrong name: drink 2.
New rule: everyone must speak in a fake accent of their choice — decide now and commit. Break character: drink 2.
New rule: nobody can say "yes" or "no." Use "affirmative," "negative," "indeed," "absolutely not" — or get creative. Say the banned words: drink 2.
New rule: {STARTER} is the Thumb Master. When they put their thumb on the table, everyone must follow — last to put theirs down drinks 2.
New rule: everyone must address each other formally — "Mr." or "Ms." followed by their last name. Use first names or nicknames: drink 2.
The no-names rule is over. {A} picks the person who came up with the best nickname tonight — they hand out 3 sips.
The accent rule is done. {A} votes for the most committed performer — they give out 3 sips. Worst accent: drink 2.
The yes/no ban is lifted. {A} picks whoever slipped up the most — they drink 3. If nobody slipped up: {A} gives out 3 sips.
The Thumb Master rule ends. {A} names the person who reacted fastest overall — they get to hand out 4 sips.
Formalities are dropped. {A} picks who played the role most convincingly — they give out 3 sips. Most out-of-character: drink 2.
